questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Italy and would like to learn more about the culture and become a part of it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Milan is great - huge recommendation from me:)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The website of University of Milan is very confusing, so I was very confused before arrivel, but I was sent the most important things by email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not really receive any assistance, but I had a contact person from Unimi, who I could write to and step by his office, but I could have used more information in the beginning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There where no introduction or any activities for new international students, which was very disappointing.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy to find something, but very hard to find something that is not very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I used
spotahome.com
, which was easy to use and find something, but there are A LOT of fees to pay for everything, so be aware. Just in general be aware of scammers, there are a lot of the, in Milan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would have love that the university had more campus options or helped the students, but none of this unfortunately

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So complicated to find courses available, took me forever. And so few courses in english (on my study subject)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Cant even describe all of it, but I had to find courses and send to the host institution and they had to approve that they where available. But when I first has it all in place, it went quite easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A contact person from university of Milan, who was nice to help, but didnt always answer all questions or understood the problem. But he was nice and it all worked out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull when I first found the courses available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take a deep look into the course catalogue and make sure which tri- og semester the course is available at and which faculty your subject is placed under, it has a lot to say about when you have to start your trimester or semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very low academic level

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Everything was much lower level than at UCPH. Everything from reading, lectures, exams ect. was very easy. I would say the level of the MA at UNIMI was lower than the BA at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lecturing and less group work. But a lot of discussion in class, more that at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marketing (Advanced)
Human Resources Management
Consumer Culture
Digital Cultures and Communication Research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Digital Cultures and Communication Research because the teacher (Gandini) was very good and the course was interesting even though it was a low level.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Just that the rent is so much higher than expected and in generel Milan is a very expensive city

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The rent is so much higher than expected and in generel Milan is a very expensive city. Coffee is cheaper than expected - but that is about the only thing (also some types of food).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not find any. They are not very good at getting international students involved in such things or maybe I just missed it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are some group chats with Erasmus students, which have a lot of activities, but not really anything from the university itself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Follow @daysofmilan on Instagram and check out her recommendation for Milan

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Aperitivo and a lot of it - Milan has the best aperitivo (when you go out for drinks after school/work and get free snacks). Visit Navigli for drinks and try all the delicious restaurants in Milan.
Also go to Lake Como.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, great food and great wine - easy to adapt to. But italians take everything very slow and easy, they are never on time and transport is not to trust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really, they keep a lot to themselves. But if you ask anything they are very nice!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Them not being on time and generally they have low situational awareness, which can be annoying. Also they talk a lot in class when the teacher is speaking, very rude.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The part about never stressing and always being kind to new people. And of course the food, the best part of Italy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Save money before, rent is expensive and you will eat your money up in great food and drinks!
2. Be openminded to new people and say yes to new things
3. Enjoy - once in a lifetime to be able to life your best life in Italy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check in good time when the trimester or semester starts, it changes from faculty to faculty

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends for life <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The economic part - more expensive than expected.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Milan - it's worth it :)))

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
